title: Private deployments: VPC & On‑Prem deployment guide, reference architectures, day‑2 ops, and upgrade/rollback
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's standard guidance for private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem packaged installs). It covers target reference architectures, packaging options, customer requirements checklists, day-2 operational runbooks, and first-class upgrade and rollback procedures. Intended audience: SREs, Platform Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and Customer Success engineers supporting Private deployments.

Table of contents
1) Introduction and scope
2) Reference architectures (VPC and on‑prem)
3) Packaging and delivery options
4) Customer requirements library (pre‑sales and onboarding checklist)
5) Day‑2 operations (monitoring, backups, incident playbook)
6) Upgrade and rollback procedures (canary -> cluster rollback)
7) Ownership, SLAs and SLOs
8) Appendices: sample terraform snippets, network diagrams, and runbook commands

1) Introduction and scope
- Purpose: Provide a single source of truth for consistent, repeatable private deployments that meet Redwood's production reliability and security expectations.
- Scope: This doc applies to deployments of Redwood Private (control plane + runtime) in customer VPCs, and on‑prem installs where the customer manages the hardware and network. It assumes the customer has committed to a supported deployment contract and that the deployment is performed by Redwood SRE or a certified partner.

2) Reference architectures (VPC and on‑prem)
- High level patterns:
  - VPC-hosted (preferred for cloud-native customers): Customer provisions cloud resources in their VPC. Redwood provides a control-plane endpoint, manifests, and IaC templates.
  - On‑prem (air-gapped or regulated): Appliance-style packaging delivered as OCI images + tarball with installer; includes Helm charts for K8s or systemd service bundles for bare-metal.

- Core logical components (both patterns):
  - Control Plane (optional managed or customer-hosted) — services: ie. control-api, auth-proxy, audit-logger.
  - Serving Runtime — GPU/CPU workloads, model-store, inference-workers, autoscaler.
  - Observability — Prometheus exporters, Grafana, tracing (Jaeger/OTLP).
  - Storage — object store (S3 compatible) for model artifacts and blob cache; metadata DB (Postgres).
  - Networking — private endpoints, DNS, TLS termination, egress controls.

- Reference VPC topology (recommended):
  - Subnets: management (private), serving (private), egress (nat).
  - Route table rules: internal-only control plane CIDR, restricted egress via proxy.
  - Security groups/NACLs: permit only required ports (API 443, metrics 9090, internal gRPC/TCP ranges).
  - Example components placement: control plane in management subnet; inference GPU pools in serving subnet(s) pinned to specific AZs for hardware locality.

- On‑Prem topology notes:
  - Hardware: GPU nodes (NVIDIA A100/A10s) in a dedicated VLAN; management + storage nodes in separate VLAN.
  - Storage: recommended Ceph or S3-compatible object gateway for model artifacts.
  - Time sync: NTP across all nodes (chrony recommended).
  - Air gap: signed OCI images and offline installer with hash verification.

3) Packaging and delivery options
- Cloud‑VPC distribution:
  - Terraform modules (recommended) with variables: cluster_name, control_plane_cidr, model_store_bucket, kms_key_arn.
  - Helm charts for Redwood services (values.yaml abstractions for external services).
  - Recommended release strategy: Semantic versioned bundles (vX.Y.Z) with image digests pinned.

- On‑Prem distribution:
  - Options: 1) Helm-based K8s package for customer K8s clusters (Rancher, OpenShift supported), 2) Appliance tarball for bare-metal with systemd services.
  - Delivery artifacts: signed release tar.gz, checksums (.sha256), and installer binary.
  - Packaging constraints: image caching proxy, offline package manifest (manifest.json), and hardware compatibility matrix.

4) Customer requirements library (pre‑sales & onboarding checklist)
- Network & Security (minimum):
  - VPC CIDR allocation and subnet plan.
  - Public IPs: none required for control plane if private peering is used.
  - TLS termination strategy and cert provisioning (ACME or customer-managed certs).
  - KMS/HSM access: ARN or connection info for key wrapping.
  - Egress policy: list of allowed egress endpoints (for telemetry, package updates, Redfish/BMC if applicable).

- Compute & Storage:
  - GPU types and counts (example: 4x A100 40GB for initial pilot).
  - Disk sizing: model cache (1TB per 4 GPUs), logs (200GB/node), DB (managed Postgres size based on TPS).
  - Storage backend type: S3-compatible endpoint or Ceph cluster for on‑prem.

- Identity & Access:
  - Service account with least privilege for S3 and KMS operations.
  - LDAP/Okta integration details for RBAC.

- Compliance & audit:
  - Retention windows for audit logs (default 90d).
  - SIEM integration endpoints.

- Customer onboarding checklist (high-level):
  1. Confirm network diagram and required CIDRs.
  2. Validate hardware SKU and quotas.
  3. Exchange TLS certs and KMS access.
  4. Arrange jump box and remote-console access for install window.
  5. Run pre-install verification script and provide results to Redwood engineer.

5) Day‑2 operations (monitoring, backups, incident playbook)
- Monitoring and alerting (minimum baseline):
  - Metrics to track: token_latency_p95, request_errors_rate, model_cache_hit_ratio, gpu_memory_utilization, queue_depth.
  - Alert thresholds (examples):
    - token_latency_p95 > 1.5s for 5m -> P1 (SRE paged)
    - request_errors_rate > 2% for 5m -> P1
    - model_cache_hit_ratio < 40% for 10m -> P2
    - gpu_memory_utilization > 90% -> P2
  - Dashboards: per-cluster latency/cost, per-route error breakdown, rolling 24h request traces.

- Backups and recovery:
  - Postgres backups: hourly WAL shipping to S3 (retain 7 days; daily snapshots retained 30d).
  - Model artifacts: immutable object-store with versioned keys.
  - Recovery RPO/RTO targets: RPO = 1h, RTO = 4h for non-critical infra; agreements vary per customer.

- Routine maintenance tasks (weekly/monthly):
  - Weekly: rotate TLS certs due within 30 days; check model-store object integrity; verify Prometheus target coverage.
  - Monthly: prune old release images, verify DB vacuuming and indices, run load test on a canary path.

- Incident response playbook (summary):
  1. Triage: route alerts to oncall SRE, attach runbook ID.
  2. Containment: identify affected pool (control plane vs runtime GPU pool).
  3. Mitigation: scale up fallback GPU pool or switch traffic to an alternative region/model variant.
  4. Recovery: restore DB from snapshot if metadata corruption; redeploy affected services.
  5. Postmortem: complete within 5 business days; include impact timeline and corrective action.

6) Upgrade and rollback procedures (canary -> cluster rollback)
- Principles:
  - All upgrades should be staged: unit -> canary -> gradual rollout -> full rollout.
  - Use image digests (immutable) and migration lockstep for DB schema changes.
  - Maintain a tested rollback artifact for each release.

- Pre-upgrade checklist:
  - Confirm pre-upgrade health: all nodes Ready, error_rate < 0.5%, token_latency_p95 within baseline.
  - Ensure backups: final Postgres snapshot + WAL upload and object-store snapshot.
  - Notify stakeholders and schedule an approved maintenance window if > 5% expected impact.

- Canary procedure (example):
  1. Deploy release vX.Y.Z to a single canary namespace/cluster with 5–10% traffic routing.
  2. Run smoke tests: basic generation, embeddings, auth, and public metrics scrape.
  3. Monitor canary for 30–60 minutes for latency, errors, and model quality regressions (run a short eval prompt set).
  4. If canary passes, increase rollout to 25% for 1 hour, then 50%, then 100% with pauses between stages.

- Rollback procedure (immediate):
  - If canary or any stage exhibits P1/P0 behavior: abort rollout and execute rollback to previous image digest on affected nodes.
  - Rollback steps (summary):
    1. Pause rollout controller (e.g., set rollout.pause=true).
    2. Re-deploy previous release manifest (image digests pinned) to affected namespaces.
    3. Verify service health and run smoke tests.
    4. If DB schema was changed, follow the backward-compatible migration policy: do not attempt incompatible DB downgrades in rollback — contact Platform lead.

- Post-upgrade validation checklist:
  - Confirm metric baselines: latency, error rate, throughput.
  - Run regression prompt-set and compare against baseline scores.
  - Capture trace samples and ensure upstream clients see no schema/contract changes.

7) Ownership, SLAs and SLOs
- Ownership matrix (examples):
  - Redwood SRE: overall deployment observability, upgrade orchestration, and incident postmortems.
  - Customer Platform team: physical hardware, network ACLs, and KMS/HSM operation.
  - Redwood Solutions Engineering: initial install verification, model onboarding assistance.

- Example SLOs for Private deployments (configure in contract):
  - Control plane API availability: 99.9% monthly (exclusions for agreed maintenance windows).
  - Single-region inference latency SLO: 95th percentile completion < 600ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) under baseline load.
  - Error budget and escalation: error budget burn rate > 50% in 24h -> escalate to Engineering leadership.

8) Appendices
- Network example table:
  | Component | Port | Proto | Notes |
  | Control Plane API | 443 | TCP | Allow from customer-admin CIDR only |
  | Metrics | 9090 | TCP | Allow from monitoring cluster or central Prometheus |
  | Inference (gRPC) | 50051 | TCP | Internal only between runtime nodes |

- Sample terraform variable snippet (example):
  ```hcl
  module "redwood_private" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/private-terraform.git//modules/cluster"
    cluster_name = var.cluster_name
    control_plane_cidr = var.control_plane_cidr
    model_store_bucket = var.model_store_bucket
    kms_key_arn = var.kms_key_arn
  }
  ```

- CLI/runbook commands (common):
  - Pre-install verification script: `./scripts/preinstall-check.sh --output=preinstall.json`
  - Tail runtime logs: `kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=inference-worker --follow --tail=200`
  - Promote canary traffic: `kubectl apply -f rollout-stage-2.yaml`
  - Force rollback: `kubectl set image deployment/inference-worker inference-worker=sha256:<previous_digest>`

Contact & escalation
- Oncall: redwood-sre-oncall (PagerDuty)
- Deployment lead (email): solutions@redwood.ai
- For legal/compliance questions: security-compliance@redwood.ai

FAQ (short)
Q: Can we perform rolling upgrades without downtime?
A: Yes—if DB migrations are backward-compatible and the rollout uses the staged canary procedure. For migrations that require downtime, coordinate maintenance windows.

Q: What is our recommended GPU for latency-sensitive workloads?
A: NVIDIA A100 80GB for highest throughput and lowest latency; A10/A100 40GB are acceptable tradeoffs for cost.
